name: John Mitchell
opening_statement: I've had this terrible crushing pain in my chest for the last hour. It's radiating down my left arm and into my jaw. I feel sweaty and nauseous.
emotional_baseline: Anxious, distressed, concerned about heart attack

socrates.onset: Sudden onset 1 hour ago while at rest watching TV
socrates.character: Crushing, heavy pressure - 'like an elephant sitting on my chest'
socrates.radiation: Radiates to left arm and jaw
socrates.exacerbating: Deep breathing makes it slightly worse
socrates.relieving: Not relieved by rest or GTN spray (2 puffs tried)

rag_citation.source: eTG Cardiovascular 2.1.1: Acute Coronary Syndrome - STEMI
rag_citation.quote: Typical chest pain in STEMI: retrosternal crushing pain with radiation to arm/jaw, associated with diaphoresis and nausea
Autonomic symptoms in ACS include diaphoresis, nausea, and vomiting
Dyspnea may accompany chest pain in acute MI, indicating left ventricular dysfunction

family_history: Father died aged 58 from myocardial infarction (MI). Mother alive, has hypertension.

social_history.smoking: Ex-smoker - quit 5 years ago, 30 pack-year history (1 pack/day × 30 years)
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife, independent with ADLs

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, JVP not elevated, peripheral pulses present bilaterally
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear breath sounds bilaterally, no creps
examination_findings.ecg: ST elevation 3mm in leads II, III, aVF (inferior STEMI), reciprocal ST depression in leads I, aVL

investigations.ecg: ST elevation ≥2mm in ≥2 contiguous leads (II, III, aVF) - diagnostic of STEMI
investigations.ue: Check renal function (creatinine for contrast studies)

expected_management: Aspirin 300mg STAT (chewed, not swallowed) - loading dose
Morphine 2.5-5mg IV for pain relief + metoclopramide 10mg IV (anti-emetic)
Primary PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) within 90 minutes door-to-balloon time
If PCI unavailable: Thrombolysis (tenecteplase or streptokinase) within 30 minutes
Transfer to cardiac catheterization lab for coronary angiography ± stent
Post-PCI: Dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel) for 12 months
Secondary prevention: ACE inhibitor, beta-blocker, statin, cardiac rehabilitation

critical_errors.error: Missed STEMI diagnosis (failed to recognize chest pain with ST elevation as ACS)
critical_errors.explanation: Delaying STEMI diagnosis increases mortality - immediate recognition required

critical_errors.error: Delayed aspirin administration (aspirin not given within first 5 minutes)
critical_errors.explanation: Aspirin reduces mortality in STEMI - immediate administration is Class I recommendation

critical_errors.error: Wrong aspirin dose (prescribed 100mg instead of 300mg loading dose)
critical_errors.explanation: Loading dose should be 300mg (chewed), not 100mg maintenance dose

critical_errors.error: Failed to activate STEMI protocol (no Code STEMI alert)
critical_errors.explanation: STEMI protocol ensures timely PCI (door-to-balloon <90 min)

fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Excellent - classic inferior STEMI presentation with all key features
fracp_reviews.difficulty_appropriate: Yes - Medium difficulty appropriate for STEMI (8 symptoms, 3 comorbidities)
fracp_reviews.rag_citations_correct: Yes - eTG 2.1 citations verified and accurate
fracp_reviews.feedback: Excellent persona. Classic presentation. Consider adding GRACE score for risk stratification (predicts 6-month mortality). Also mention troponin timing (0h, 3h, 6h) for completeness.

fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Accurate STEMI management pathway - appropriate for AMC Clinical Examination
fracp_reviews.feedback: Good persona. Emergency management correct (aspirin, clopidogrel, PCI). Suggest adding brief mention of contraindications to thrombolysis (recent surgery, active bleeding, etc.) for completeness.

learning_objectives: Recognize classic STEMI presentation (crushing chest pain + ST elevation)
Apply SOCRATES framework to chest pain history
Initiate immediate STEMI management (aspirin 300mg, clopidogrel, STEMI activation)
Understand door-to-balloon time importance (<90 minutes for primary PCI)
Identify cardiovascular risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, smoking, family history)
